title: Minimum Time to Break Locks II
exampleStatus: Source examples not copied; worked illustrations are independently authored in clarification.
summary: Energy starts at zero and grows by X each minute, initially X=1. A lock can break once energy reaches its strength. Breaking resets energy to zero and increments X by exactly one. Choose any lock order and return minimum total minutes. There is no separate K increment input in this variant.
clarification: Derived cost for the j-th lock (one-based) is ceil(strength/j); minimize the sum over permutations. Authored example strengths [8,2]: breaking 2 then 8 costs 2+4=6; the other order costs 8+1=9, so answer 6.
